messages.subject: Transect data
parts:
I have a question about transect data. In the online and workshop 
materials I could find they are treated somewhat parenthetically so I want to make 
sure I understand the data input correctly.

If I missed some materials that explain this approach, I'd appreciate a push in the right direction.

First, the transects are entered as a series of x-y coordinates similar 
to the vertices of a polygon detector, correct?

If so, here are my questions:

1. Murray (2013) makes a statement in Appendix D that transects 
cannot loop back on themselves. I'm not exactly clear on the limitations 
of transect layout We had field techs generally follow a rectangle 
transect (to end up at their start point - logistically efficient) and 
record a tracklog of their path. However, that was a general guideline 
because we needed them to search for quality scat samples (for DNA) so I 
allowed them to deviate as they thought appropriate. Do I need to 
simplify this path into a series of straight-line paths that do not 
cross over themselves? Is that sufficient?

2. If I simplify the transects, I then have to make sure the locations 
of where deer pellets are detected fall exactly on the transect line, 
correct? In my situation, I don't think any error introduced by doing 
this will affect density estimates because the individual transects are smaller 
than the home range of a deer and there are multiple transects.

3. Is there another way to skin this cat? For example, could I make the 
transect a series of point detectors and simply assign a scat detection 
to the nearest detector? If so, any rule of thumb on distance between 
detectors?  Transects are about 0.5 km long and spaced several km apart.


Thanks,

Duane

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Transect data
parts:
On your first question, input of transect data should follow the pattern for polygon data: x-y coords of each detection are provided in columns 4,5 of the capture file and fmt = 'XY' (see secr-datainput.pdf).

My reticience about the 'transect' detector type is based on (i) never having used it in anger myself (ii) knowing that the probability model has an assumption (detection rate/probability scales with the length of transect intersecting the home range UD) that is potentially violated if the transect is wiggly, with unknown effects, and (iii) knowing that some fairly tortuous programming was involved.

I am very comfortable with your third point: modelling transect detectors as a series of point detectors. I have added a function 'discretize' for polygons in 2.10.0, and maybe should look at the same for transects.

If your individual transects are smaller than the home range of a deer, are you relying on re-detections between transects to get the home-range scale? It seems you could use quite coarse discretization within transects without losing information.

 Murray
